title: Wave-based control-plane version rollout: Terraform orchestration and canary gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Private control planes must be upgradable with minimal blast radius and clear rollback paths. Current upgrades are manual, slow, and risky for customers running in VPCs. This ticket delivers a Terraform-driven, wave-based rollout orchestration that performs immutable control-plane node replacements in small waves, validates health via synthetic probes and real traffic sampling, and can auto-abort/rollback on defined health regressions. The implementation will integrate with existing upgrade orchestration hooks, the control plane version registry, and the deployment audit log for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module 'controlplane/wave-rollout' can create a rollout plan and apply wave replacements without manual SSH/console steps
Canary wave defined as configurable percent (default 5%) of control-plane nodes and a health gate evaluated via synthetic probes + request-level SLOs
Automated rollback triggers on any of: increased 5xx rate > baseline +2% for 5m, median RPC latency > baseline * 1.5 for 5m, or control-plane internal readiness failing > 1 node in wave
Audit trail in control-plane audit log showing version changes, wave IDs, who triggered rollout, and Terraform apply IDs
End-to-end test harness that runs against an internal staging VPC and simulates a 3-wave rollout with induced failure on wave 2 and verifies rollback
Documentation in Confluence and a console-facing rollout summary view is available for the release
implementation_plan: Design Terraform module with resources: rollout.plan (S3/State entry), rollout.wave (counted), rollout.action (immutable replacement) and hooks for pre/post health checks
Add control-plane agent endpoint to drain new node readiness and emit 'upgrade-progress' events to the control-plane event bus

Implement health gate evaluator service that consumes synthetic probe results and real-metrics from metrics-ingest (Prometheus) and exposes a stable API consumed by Terraform via external data provider
Build rollback orchestration: mark unhealthy wave, trigger immutably created replacement with previous version image, and cancel remaining waves
Add RBAC checks so only release engineers and CI pipelines can trigger non-automated rollouts; all manual triggers must require two approvers
Write a canary-to-production policy: waves: [5%, 25%, 100%] by default with configurable wait windows and exponential backoff on transient failures
test_plan: Unit tests for Terraform module via terratest: validate plan generation and external data calls
Integration test that runs a full rollout in staging VPC with a fake metrics backend to validate health gating and auto-rollback
Chaos test: during wave 2, inject 50% RPC error on a subset of control-plane replicas and confirm rollback triggers and system recovers
Load test: synthetic probes + 1k requests/min sampled against canary wave to ensure latency baselines remain within SLO
Security review and threat model for upgrade APIs and state artifacts (ensure no secrets are written to state files)
rollout_strategy: Wave-based immutable replacements with pre-defined waves (default 5/25/100). Health gates incorporate both synthetic probes (probe-runner) and production-sampled request metrics. Terraform applies only create new nodes; replacement is signaled via 'drain-and-retire' lifecycle hook. Auto-abort triggers create a stop record and invoke rollback module to provision previous-version instances.
monitoring_playbook: Dashboard: controlplane/upgrade-waves showing per-wave health, latency, error rate, and node readiness
Alert: upgrade.health-gate-failed -> P0 escalation to on-call, automatic rollback execution started

Runbook steps: (1) Confirm logs in controlplane/audit, (2) Check synthetic-probe details, (3) If transient, extend wait-window x1.5 once, (4) If persistent, allow automated rollback to continue and open postmortem
Post-rollback verification: confirm all control-plane nodes are at prior version and customer-facing endpoints are healthy for 30 minutes
comments: 2025-02-14 Aisha Patel: Initial RFC posted. Key decision: prefer immutable replacement vs in-place binary swap to simplify rollback and avoid state drift.
2025-02-20 Marco Liu: Prototype Terraform module created in feature branch. Using external data provider for health_gate API to avoid embedding secrets in state. PR: gh#482
2025-02-27 Elena Kim (SRE): Reviewed health gate thresholds. Suggested adding a 'cooldown' period between waves to reduce flapping for noisy metrics.

2025-03-03 Security review by Rajesh Mehta: flagged potential risk of long-lived credentials in provider plugin. Action: rotate provider token per-rollout and store ephemeral token in vault. Assigned: Marco Liu
2025-03-05 Marco Liu: Implemented cooldown and ephemeral token flow in terraform module, updated terratest cases. Running staging integration now.
notes: Trade-offs considered: faster 10% canary vs more conservative 5% default. We chose conservative default to minimize customer impact for initial rollout.

We intentionally keep rollout orchestration in Terraform to leverage existing state tracking and auditability; longer-term we may extract a small controller if Terraform external providers become limiting.
Make sure to coordinate with Sales/Support before enabling auto-rollback policies for enterprise customers with strict change windows.
